condition.meniscus-tear.summary: A tear in the shock-absorbing cartilage of the knee. It can happen when the knee is twisted or over-flexed, and the meniscus becomes more brittle and easier to tear with age.
condition.meniscus-tear.location: Each knee has two C-shaped menisci cushioning the bones of the joint.
condition.meniscus-tear.not_depicted: The tear and knee motion are not depicted.

condition.knee-osteoarthritis.title: Osteoarthritis of the knee
condition.knee-osteoarthritis.summary: A degenerative joint disease in which tissues of the joint break down over time. It is the most common disease affecting the knee: the cartilage gradually wears away, causing pain and swelling.
condition.knee-osteoarthritis.location: Articular cartilage covers the ends of the thigh bone and shin bone where they meet at the knee.
condition.knee-osteoarthritis.not_depicted: Cartilage loss, bone spurs and joint changes are not depicted.

condition.heart-attack.title: Heart attack
condition.heart-attack.summary: Blood flow that brings oxygen to part of the heart muscle suddenly becomes blocked. If blood flow is not restored quickly, the heart muscle begins to die. Most heart attacks are caused by coronary artery disease.
condition.heart-attack.location: The coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta and supply the heart muscle.
condition.heart-attack.not_depicted: Blocked arteries, blood flow and damaged heart muscle are not depicted.

condition.heart-failure.title: Heart failure
condition.heart-failure.summary: The heart doesn't pump enough blood for the body's needs, or is too weak to pump properly. Also called congestive heart failure, it is most often caused by another condition that damages the heart, and needs medical care.
condition.heart-failure.location: The heart pumps blood through the lungs and the body.
condition.heart-failure.not_depicted: Weakened pumping and blood flow are not depicted.

condition.atrial-fibrillation.title: Atrial fibrillation
condition.atrial-fibrillation.summary: The heart beats irregularly and sometimes much faster than normal, and its upper and lower chambers do not work together as they should. Blood may pool in the heart, raising the risk of clots and stroke.
condition.atrial-fibrillation.location: The atria are the heart's two upper chambers.
condition.atrial-fibrillation.not_depicted: Heart rhythm, pooled blood and clots are not depicted.

condition.pneumonia.title: Pneumonia
condition.pneumonia.summary: An infection that affects one or both lungs. It causes the air sacs of the lungs to fill up with fluid or pus.
condition.pneumonia.location: The bronchi branch into smaller and smaller airways that end in the tiny air sacs of both lungs.
condition.pneumonia.not_depicted: Infection and fluid-filled air sacs are not depicted.

condition.lung-cancer.title: Lung cancer
condition.lung-cancer.summary: Lung cancer has two main types: non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer. Smoking causes most lung cancers, but nonsmokers can also develop it.
condition.lung-cancer.location: The right lung has three lobes and the left lung two.
condition.lung-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.ckd.title: Chronic kidney disease
condition.ckd.summary: The kidneys are damaged or have a problem with their structure and can't filter blood the way they should. Diabetes and high blood pressure are the most common causes in adults.
condition.ckd.location: The kidneys lie just below the rib cage, one on each side of the spine.
condition.ckd.not_depicted: Kidney damage and reduced filtering are not depicted.

condition.bladder-infection.title: Bladder infection (cystitis)
condition.bladder-infection.summary: An illness most often caused by bacteria that enter the bladder and multiply. It is the most common type of urinary tract infection and, if untreated, can spread to the kidneys.
condition.bladder-infection.location: The bladder, in the pelvic cavity, is a temporary storage reservoir for urine.
condition.bladder-infection.not_depicted: Infection and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.diverticular-disease.title: Diverticulosis and diverticulitis
condition.diverticular-disease.summary: In diverticulosis, small pouches form and push outward through weak spots in the wall of the colon, mostly in the sigmoid colon. Most people with these pouches have no symptoms. Diverticulitis occurs when the pouches become inflamed.
condition.diverticular-disease.location: The sigmoid colon is the lower part of the colon, just before the rectum.
condition.diverticular-disease.not_depicted: Pouches and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.crohns.title: Crohn's disease
condition.crohns.summary: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease in which abnormal immune reactions cause inflammation in the digestive tract. It most commonly affects the small intestine and the beginning of the large intestine, but can affect any part from mouth to anus.
condition.crohns.location: The ileum is the last part of the small intestine, joining the large intestine at the ileocecal junction.
condition.crohns.not_depicted: Inflammation and damage to the intestinal wall are not depicted.

condition.ulcerative-colitis.title: Ulcerative colitis
condition.ulcerative-colitis.summary: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease in which abnormal immune reactions cause inflammation and ulcers on the inner lining of the large intestine. Symptoms come and go, with flares and periods of remission.
condition.ulcerative-colitis.location: The large intestine includes the cecum, colon and rectum.
condition.ulcerative-colitis.not_depicted: Inflammation and ulcers are not depicted.

condition.celiac.title: Celiac disease
condition.celiac.summary: A chronic digestive and immune disorder that damages the small intestine. It is triggered by eating foods containing gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley and rye.
condition.celiac.location: The small intestine has three parts: the duodenum, jejunum and ileum.
condition.celiac.not_depicted: Damage to the intestinal lining is not depicted.

condition.nafld.title: Fatty liver disease (NAFLD / MASLD)
condition.nafld.summary: Excess fat builds up in the liver, not caused by heavy alcohol use. It is also called metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
condition.nafld.location: The liver lies mainly in the upper right abdomen, just beneath the diaphragm.
condition.nafld.not_depicted: Fat buildup and changes in liver tissue are not depicted.

condition.viral-hepatitis.title: Viral hepatitis
condition.viral-hepatitis.summary: An infection that causes liver inflammation and damage. Several different viruses cause it, including hepatitis A, B, C, D and E.
condition.viral-hepatitis.location: The liver lies mainly in the upper right abdomen, just beneath the diaphragm.
condition.viral-hepatitis.not_depicted: Inflammation and liver damage are not depicted.

condition.diabetes.title: Diabetes
condition.diabetes.summary: Blood glucose (blood sugar) is too high. Insulin, a hormone made by the pancreas, helps glucose get into cells for energy. In diabetes the body doesn't make enough or any insulin, or doesn't use it properly.
condition.diabetes.location: The pancreas releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine and hormones such as insulin into the blood.
condition.diabetes.not_depicted: Blood glucose and insulin are not depicted.

condition.hemorrhoids.title: Hemorrhoids
condition.hemorrhoids.summary: Swollen and inflamed veins around the anus or in the lower rectum, also called piles. They are common, affecting about half of adults older than 50.
condition.hemorrhoids.location: The rectum is the end of the large intestine, continuing to the anal canal.

condition.colorectal-cancer.title: Colorectal cancer
condition.colorectal-cancer.summary: Often begins as a growth called a polyp inside the colon or rectum. Finding and removing polyps can prevent colorectal cancer.
condition.colorectal-cancer.location: The colon is the main part of the large intestine; the rectum continues from the sigmoid colon.
condition.colorectal-cancer.not_depicted: Polyps and tumors are not depicted.

condition.fibroids.title: Uterine fibroids
condition.fibroids.summary: Growths made of smooth muscle cells and other tissue that grow in or on the wall of the uterus. They can cause pain and abnormal bleeding.
condition.fibroids.location: The uterus is a muscular organ in which a fetus develops.

condition.pcos.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
condition.pcos.summary: A set of metabolic and reproductive symptoms related to a hormonal imbalance. It may cause menstrual changes, skin changes, growths in one or both ovaries and infertility.
condition.pcos.location: The ovaries lie on each side of the uterus in the side walls of the pelvic cavity.
condition.pcos.not_depicted: Follicle growths and hormone levels are not depicted.

condition.cervical-cancer.title: Cervical cancer
condition.cervical-cancer.summary: Cancer that starts in the cells of the cervix. It usually develops slowly: before cancer appears, cells of the cervix go through abnormal changes known as dysplasia.
condition.cervical-cancer.location: The cervix is the lower, narrow end of the uterus and connects it to the vagina.
condition.cervical-cancer.not_depicted: Abnormal cells and tumors are not depicted.

condition.prostate-cancer.title: Prostate cancer
condition.prostate-cancer.summary: The most common cancer among men in the United States. It usually grows very slowly.
condition.prostate-cancer.location: The prostate lies just below the bladder and surrounds the part of the urethra just below it.
condition.prostate-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.retinal-detachment.title: Retinal detachment
condition.retinal-detachment.summary: The retina is pulled away from its normal position at the back of the eye. Larger detachments can cause sudden symptoms such as many new floaters, flashes of light, or a shadow over part of the vision.
condition.retinal-detachment.location: The retina is the light-sensitive layer of tissue at the back of the eye.
condition.retinal-detachment.not_depicted: The detached retina is not depicted.

condition.psoriasis.title: Psoriasis
condition.psoriasis.summary: An immune-mediated disease: overactive immune cells set off rapid production of skin cells. Patches of skin become scaly and inflamed, most often on the scalp, elbows or knees.
condition.psoriasis.location: The skin covers the entire outside of the body.
condition.psoriasis.not_depicted: Skin patches and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.atopic-dermatitis.title: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
condition.atopic-dermatitis.summary: A common, non-contagious condition that usually begins in childhood. It makes the skin extremely itchy, with red, dry patches.
condition.atopic-dermatitis.location: The skin covers the entire outside of the body.

condition.skin-cancer.title: Skin cancer
condition.skin-cancer.summary: The main types are squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma and melanoma.
condition.skin-cancer.location: The epidermis, the skin's tough outer layer, contains the melanin-producing melanocytes.
condition.skin-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and skin changes are not depicted.

condition.uveitis.title: Uveitis
condition.uveitis.summary: Inflammation inside the eye. It damages the uvea, made of the iris, ciliary body and choroid, and often affects other parts of the eye too.
condition.uveitis.location: The uvea's three parts are the iris, the ciliary body and the choroid.

condition.pink-eye.title: Pink eye (conjunctivitis)
condition.pink-eye.summary: Swelling and redness of the inside of the eyelid and the white part of the eye. It is common, and most often caused by a virus or bacteria; some types spread very easily.
condition.pink-eye.location: The supplied eyes include the eyelid lining and the white of the eye.
condition.pink-eye.not_depicted: Swelling and redness are not depicted.

condition.floaters.title: Floaters
condition.floaters.summary: Small dark shapes that float across the vision. With age, tiny strands of the vitreous stick together and cast shadows on the retina.
condition.floaters.location: The vitreous is the gel-like fluid that fills the eye.
condition.floaters.not_depicted: The strands and their shadows are not depicted.

condition.bladder-cancer.title: Bladder cancer
condition.bladder-cancer.summary: Almost all bladder cancers are urothelial carcinomas, which begin in the cells lining the bladder. Muscle-invasive cancer has spread through the lining into the bladder's muscle wall.
condition.bladder-cancer.location: The bladder is a hollow organ in the pelvis that stores urine.
condition.bladder-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and the bladder lining are not depicted.

condition.osteoporosis.title: Osteoporosis
condition.osteoporosis.summary: A bone disease in which bone mineral density and mass decrease, or bone structure and strength change, raising the risk of fractures. It is often "silent" until a bone breaks; fractures happen most often in the hip, spine and wrist.
condition.osteoporosis.location: The supplied pelvis shows compact and spongy bone tissue. Fractures can occur in any bone.
condition.osteoporosis.not_depicted: Loss of bone density and fractures are not depicted.

condition.pancreatic-cancer.title: Pancreatic cancer
condition.pancreatic-cancer.summary: Pancreatic cancer can develop from two kinds of cells in the pancreas: exocrine cells and endocrine cells (pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors).
condition.pancreatic-cancer.location: The pancreas releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine and hormones such as insulin into the blood.
condition.pancreatic-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.liver-cancer.title: Liver cancer
condition.liver-cancer.summary: Cancer that starts in the liver is called primary liver cancer. The most common type in adults is hepatocellular carcinoma.
condition.liver-cancer.location: The liver lies mainly in the upper right abdomen, just beneath the diaphragm.
condition.liver-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.kidney-cancer.title: Kidney cancer
condition.kidney-cancer.summary: Kidney cancer can develop in adults and children. The main types are renal cell cancer, transitional cell cancer and Wilms tumor.
condition.kidney-cancer.location: The kidneys lie just below the rib cage, one on each side of the spine.
condition.kidney-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.ovarian-cancer.title: Ovarian cancer
condition.ovarian-cancer.summary: Ovarian epithelial cancer, Fallopian tube cancer and primary peritoneal cancer form in the same kind of tissue and are treated the same way. These cancers are often advanced when diagnosed.
condition.ovarian-cancer.location: The ovaries lie one on each side of the uterus, in the side walls of the pelvic cavity.
condition.ovarian-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.uterine-cancer.title: Uterine cancer
condition.uterine-cancer.summary: Uterine cancers are of two types: endometrial cancer, which is common and can often be cured, and uterine sarcoma, which is rare and often more aggressive.
condition.uterine-cancer.location: The uterus is a muscular organ in which a fetus develops.
condition.uterine-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.brain-tumors.title: Brain tumors
condition.brain-tumors.summary: Tumors of the brain and spinal cord (the central nervous system) can be benign or malignant, and there are many different types.
condition.brain-tumors.location: The brain is divided into the cerebrum, diencephalon, brain stem and cerebellum.

condition.pulmonary-hypertension.title: Pulmonary hypertension
condition.pulmonary-hypertension.summary: A condition that affects the blood vessels in the lungs. In the United States its most common type is caused by left-sided heart disease, such as left heart failure.
condition.pulmonary-hypertension.location: The pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs.
condition.pulmonary-hypertension.not_depicted: Blood pressure in the lung vessels is not depicted.

condition.pkd.title: Polycystic kidney disease
condition.pkd.summary: A genetic disorder that causes many fluid-filled cysts to grow in the kidneys. The cysts can change the shape of the kidneys, including making them much larger.
condition.pkd.location: The kidneys lie just below the rib cage, one on each side of the spine.
condition.pkd.not_depicted: Cysts and kidney enlargement are not depicted.

condition.lactose-intolerance.title: Lactose intolerance
condition.lactose-intolerance.summary: Digestive symptoms such as bloating, diarrhea and gas after consuming lactose, a sugar in milk and milk products. They happen because the small intestine cannot break down all the lactose eaten.
condition.lactose-intolerance.location: The small intestine has three parts: the duodenum, jejunum and ileum.
condition.lactose-intolerance.not_depicted: Digestion and symptoms are not depicted.

condition.hydrocephalus.title: Hydrocephalus
condition.hydrocephalus.summary: Too much cerebrospinal fluid builds up in the brain and puts harmful pressure on it. It can be present at birth or happen at any age, after causes such as head injuries, strokes, infections, tumors or bleeding in the brain.
condition.hydrocephalus.location: Cerebrospinal fluid is made in the brain's ventricles and flows in and around the hollow spaces of the brain and spinal cord.
condition.hydrocephalus.not_depicted: Excess fluid, enlarged ventricles and pressure are not depicted.

condition.meningitis.title: Meningitis
condition.meningitis.summary: Inflammation of the meninges, the thin tissue surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Viral meningitis is the most common type; bacterial meningitis is rare but can be deadly.
condition.meningitis.location: The meninges cover the brain and spinal cord. The supplied models do not include them around the brain, so the brain is shown.
condition.meningitis.not_depicted: The meninges and their inflammation are not depicted.

condition.tbi.title: Traumatic brain injury
condition.tbi.summary: A sudden injury that damages the brain, from a blow, bump or jolt to the head or an object that penetrates the skull. Concussions are a type of mild TBI; severe TBI can cause coma or death.
condition.tbi.location: The brain is divided into the cerebrum, diencephalon, brain stem and cerebellum.
condition.tbi.not_depicted: Injury and brain damage are not depicted.

condition.strabismus.title: Strabismus (crossed eyes)
condition.strabismus.summary: The six muscles around each eye normally work as a team so both eyes focus on the same object. In strabismus they do not, so one eye turns in a different direction. In children, untreated strabismus can lead to amblyopia (lazy eye).
condition.strabismus.location: The six muscles that move each eye lie in the orbit around the eyeball.

condition.ptosis.title: Ptosis (drooping eyelid)
condition.ptosis.summary: A drooping upper eyelid, one of the common eyelid disorders.
condition.ptosis.location: The levator palpebrae superioris is the only muscle that raises the upper eyelid.
condition.ptosis.not_depicted: The eyelids and their drooping are not depicted.

condition.retinal-artery-occlusion.title: Retinal artery occlusion
condition.retinal-artery-occlusion.summary: A blockage of an artery of the retina, usually by a blood clot or fat deposit. Clots most often come from the heart or the carotid artery in the neck. Part or all of the retina then does not get enough blood and oxygen, and vision can be lost.
condition.retinal-artery-occlusion.location: The central retinal artery supplies the internal surface of the retina.
condition.retinal-artery-occlusion.not_depicted: The blockage and retinal damage are not depicted.

condition.voice-disorders.title: Voice disorders
condition.voice-disorders.summary: Talking too much, screaming, constant throat clearing or smoking can injure the vocal cords, causing hoarseness and problems such as nodules, polyps and sores. Infections and other conditions can also cause voice disorders.
condition.voice-disorders.location: The vocal cords are two bands of muscle in the larynx (voice box). The vocal fold muscles are supplied only in the male model.
condition.voice-disorders.not_depicted: Nodules, polyps and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.laryngitis.title: Laryngitis
condition.laryngitis.summary: Swelling and irritation of the voice box, usually caused by a virus, that causes hoarseness. Allergies, bacterial infection, GERD, injury, irritants and overuse of the voice can also cause it.
condition.laryngitis.location: The larynx sits at the top of the airway to the lungs and contains the vocal cords.
condition.laryngitis.not_depicted: Swelling and infection are not depicted.

condition.dvt.title: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
condition.dvt.summary: A blood clot in a vein deep in the body. A DVT can break loose and cause a pulmonary embolism in the lung. Sitting still for a long time makes it more likely.
condition.dvt.location: Most deep vein clots occur in the lower leg or thigh, which these models do not include. The iliac veins shown carry blood from the legs towards the heart.
condition.dvt.not_depicted: Clots and the leg veins are not depicted.

condition.multiple-sclerosis.title: Multiple sclerosis (MS)
condition.multiple-sclerosis.summary: A disease of the brain and spinal cord that damages myelin, the protective coating around nerve cells. Messages between the brain and body then slow down or are blocked.
condition.multiple-sclerosis.location: MS affects the central nervous system: the brain and spinal cord.
condition.multiple-sclerosis.not_depicted: Myelin and its damage are not depicted.

condition.migraine.title: Migraine
condition.migraine.summary: A recurring headache with moderate to severe throbbing or pulsing pain, often on one side of the head, sometimes with nausea, weakness and sensitivity to light and sound. Researchers believe it has a genetic cause; triggers vary between people.
condition.migraine.location: Migraine pain is felt in the head; the brain is shown for reference.
condition.migraine.not_depicted: Headache and its triggers are not depicted.

condition.pelvic-support-problems.title: Pelvic support problems (prolapse)
condition.pelvic-support-problems.summary: The pelvic floor holds the uterus, bladder and bowel in place. It can be weakened or injured, mainly by pregnancy and childbirth, and organs can then drop into the vagina.
condition.pelvic-support-problems.location: The uterus is also supported by its round, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments.
condition.pelvic-support-problems.not_depicted: The pelvic floor muscles and prolapse are not depicted.

condition.bile-duct-cancer.title: Bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma)
condition.bile-duct-cancer.summary: A rare disease in which cancer cells form in the bile ducts, the network of tubes connecting the liver, gallbladder and small intestine.
condition.bile-duct-cancer.location: The right and left hepatic ducts lead out of the liver and join to form the common hepatic duct.
condition.bile-duct-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.ectopic-pregnancy.title: Ectopic pregnancy
condition.ectopic-pregnancy.summary: The fertilized egg grows outside the uterus, usually in a fallopian tube. It cannot become a healthy pregnancy, and a growing pregnancy can burst the tube and cause life-threatening internal bleeding.
condition.ectopic-pregnancy.location: The fallopian tubes carry eggs from the ovaries to the uterus.
condition.ectopic-pregnancy.not_depicted: The pregnancy and bleeding are not depicted.

condition.ovarian-cysts.title: Ovarian cysts
condition.ovarian-cysts.summary: Fluid-filled sacs in or on an ovary, usually formed during ovulation. Most are small, harmless and go away by themselves. Larger cysts can cause pain or complications such as ovarian torsion.
condition.ovarian-cysts.location: The ovaries lie on each side of the uterus, attached by their suspensory ligaments and the ligaments of the ovary.

condition.spleen-diseases.title: Swollen or ruptured spleen
condition.spleen-diseases.summary: Certain diseases can make the spleen swell, and an injury can damage or rupture it, especially when it is already swollen. A badly damaged spleen may need to be removed; people can live without one.
condition.spleen-diseases.location: The spleen sits under the ribs on the left side, above the stomach.
condition.spleen-diseases.not_depicted: Swelling and injury are not depicted.

condition.male-infertility.title: Male infertility
condition.male-infertility.summary: When a man has not been able to get a partner pregnant after at least a year of trying. Causes include problems with the testicles, blockages in the ducts that carry sperm, hormone problems and genetic disorders.
condition.male-infertility.location: The vas deferens and ejaculatory ducts carry sperm. The testes are not supplied in this model.
condition.male-infertility.not_depicted: Sperm, blockages and the testes are not depicted.

condition.urethral-disorders.title: Urethral stricture and urethritis
condition.urethral-disorders.summary: Urethral problems include urethral stricture, a narrowing of the urethra, and urethritis, its inflammation, sometimes caused by infection. They can cause pain or difficulty passing urine.
condition.urethral-disorders.location: In men the urethra is a long tube that also carries semen; it begins at the bladder and passes through the prostate.
condition.urethral-disorders.not_depicted: Narrowing and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.prostatitis.title: Prostatitis
condition.prostatitis.summary: A frequently painful condition involving inflammation of the prostate and sometimes the areas around it. There are four types, including chronic pelvic pain syndrome and acute and chronic bacterial prostatitis.
condition.prostatitis.location: The prostate surrounds the part of the urethra just below the bladder.

condition.gerd.title: GERD (acid reflux disease)
condition.gerd.summary: In gastroesophageal reflux, stomach contents come back up into the esophagus, sometimes causing heartburn. GERD is a more severe, long-lasting form in which this causes repeated bothersome symptoms or leads to complications.
condition.gerd.location: The esophagus carries food down to the stomach through an opening in the diaphragm.
condition.gerd.not_depicted: Reflux and irritation are not depicted.

condition.peptic-ulcer.title: Peptic ulcer
condition.peptic-ulcer.summary: A sore on the lining of the stomach or duodenum, also called a stomach or duodenal ulcer. The two most common causes are infection with H. pylori bacteria and taking NSAIDs such as aspirin, ibuprofen and naproxen.
condition.peptic-ulcer.location: The stomach empties into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.

condition.stomach-cancer.title: Stomach cancer
condition.stomach-cancer.summary: Cancer that starts in the cells lining the stomach, also called gastric cancer. Most is adenocarcinoma, which begins in the mucus-producing cells of the innermost lining.
condition.stomach-cancer.location: The stomach lies in the upper left of the abdomen and receives food from the esophagus.
condition.stomach-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.esophageal-cancer.title: Esophageal cancer
condition.esophageal-cancer.summary: The most common types are adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma, which tend to develop in different parts of the esophagus.
condition.esophageal-cancer.location: The esophagus runs from the throat to the stomach, behind the trachea.
condition.esophageal-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.hiatal-hernia.title: Hiatal hernia
condition.hiatal-hernia.summary: The upper part of the stomach bulges through an opening in the diaphragm. This makes it easier for stomach acid to come up into the esophagus (GERD).
condition.hiatal-hernia.location: The diaphragm, the thin muscle separating the chest from the abdomen, has an opening through which the esophagus passes.

condition.hiccups.title: Hiccups
condition.hiccups.summary: An unintentional movement (spasm) of the diaphragm, the muscle at the base of the lungs. Hiccups often start for no apparent reason.
condition.hiccups.location: The diaphragm separates the chest from the abdomen.

condition.spinal-cord-injury.title: Spinal cord injury
condition.spinal-cord-injury.summary: Usually begins with a blow that breaks or dislocates vertebrae; pieces of vertebrae then tear into or press on the cord. A complete injury stops signals below the injury; with an incomplete injury some movement and feeling remain.
condition.spinal-cord-injury.location: The spinal cord runs down the middle of the back inside the vertebral column.
condition.spinal-cord-injury.not_depicted: Injury and nerve damage are not depicted.

condition.pituitary-tumors.title: Pituitary tumors
condition.pituitary-tumors.summary: Common, but often they cause no health problems and most people never know they have one. The most common type makes hormones and upsets the body's hormone balance, which can cause conditions such as Cushing syndrome.
condition.pituitary-tumors.location: The pituitary gland is a pea-sized gland at the base of the brain.

condition.adrenal-insufficiency.title: Adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease)
condition.adrenal-insufficiency.summary: The adrenal glands do not make enough of certain hormones, including cortisol, which is essential for life. The most common symptoms are fatigue, muscle weakness, loss of appetite, weight loss and abdominal pain.
condition.adrenal-insufficiency.location: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys.

condition.cushings.title: Cushing's syndrome
condition.cushings.summary: The body makes too much of the hormone cortisol over a long time. Cortisol helps the body respond to stress, maintain blood pressure and regulate blood glucose.
condition.cushings.location: The adrenal glands, two small glands on top of the kidneys, make cortisol.

condition.testicular-cancer.title: Testicular cancer
condition.testicular-cancer.summary: Most often begins in germ cells, the cells that make sperm. It is rare, most often diagnosed in men aged 20 to 34, and most cases can be cured even at an advanced stage.
condition.testicular-cancer.location: The testes lie inside the scrotum.
condition.testicular-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.erectile-dysfunction.title: Erectile dysfunction
condition.erectile-dysfunction.summary: A condition that prevents getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sex. It can often be treated.
condition.erectile-dysfunction.location: The penis contains three columns of erectile tissue.

condition.scoliosis.title: Scoliosis
condition.scoliosis.summary: A sideways curve of the spine. Children and teens with scoliosis have an abnormal S- or C-shaped curve; in most people the cause is unknown.
condition.scoliosis.location: The vertebral column runs from the base of the skull to the tailbone.

condition.herniated-disk.title: Herniated disk
condition.herniated-disk.summary: A disk between the vertebrae ruptures, letting its jelly-like center leak and irritate nearby nerves. This can cause sciatica or back pain; with treatment most people recover.
condition.herniated-disk.location: Soft disks between the vertebrae cushion them and keep them in place.
condition.herniated-disk.not_depicted: The rupture and nerve irritation are not depicted.

condition.back-pain.title: Back pain
condition.back-pain.summary: One of the most common medical problems in the United States. It becomes more common with age, particularly after 45, and is more common in people who are not physically fit.
condition.back-pain.location: The spine includes the bones, muscles, tendons and other tissues from the base of the skull to the tailbone.
condition.back-pain.not_depicted: Pain and its causes are not depicted.

condition.carpal-tunnel.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
condition.carpal-tunnel.summary: Numbness, tingling, weakness or pain in the wrist or hand when the median nerve is squeezed in the carpal tunnel, a narrow opening between the wrist bones and the ligament that holds them together.
condition.carpal-tunnel.location: The carpal tunnel lies between the bones of the wrist and the ligament that holds them together.
condition.carpal-tunnel.not_depicted: The median nerve and carpal tunnel are not depicted.

condition.gout.title: Gout
condition.gout.summary: A type of inflammatory arthritis causing pain and swelling in the joints, usually in flares that last a week or two and then resolve. Flares often begin in the big toe or a lower limb.
condition.gout.location: Each foot has tarsals, metatarsals and phalanges; flares often begin in the big toe.
condition.gout.not_depicted: Joint inflammation and crystals are not depicted.

condition.rheumatoid-arthritis.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
condition.rheumatoid-arthritis.summary: A long-lasting autoimmune disease that mostly affects joints, causing pain, swelling, stiffness and loss of function. It can affect the joints of the wrists, hands, elbows, shoulders, feet, spine, knees and jaw.
condition.rheumatoid-arthritis.location: The hands and wrists are among the joints it often affects.

condition.pad.title: Peripheral artery disease
condition.pad.summary: Plaque builds up in arteries and reduces blood flow. The most common type reduces blood flow to the legs and feet.
condition.pad.location: Branches of the external iliac arteries supply the legs.
condition.pad.not_depicted: Plaque and reduced flow are not depicted.

condition.carotid-artery-disease.title: Carotid artery disease
condition.carotid-artery-disease.summary: The carotid arteries become narrow or blocked, usually by atherosclerosis, a buildup of plaque made of fat, cholesterol, calcium and other substances.
condition.carotid-artery-disease.location: There is a carotid artery on each side of the neck, carrying blood from the heart to the head.

condition.rotator-cuff.title: Rotator cuff injuries
condition.rotator-cuff.summary: Rotator cuff injuries are common. The rotator cuff is a group of muscles and tendons that holds the top of the upper arm bone firmly in the shoulder socket and keeps the shoulder stable.
condition.rotator-cuff.location: The rotator cuff muscles connect to the humerus.
condition.rotator-cuff.not_depicted: The rotator cuff and its injury are not depicted.

condition.oral-cancer.title: Lip and oral cavity cancer
condition.oral-cancer.summary: A cancer that starts in the lips or mouth, including the front two-thirds of the tongue, the gums, the lining of the cheeks, the floor of the mouth and the hard palate.
condition.oral-cancer.location: The oral cavity contains the teeth and tongue.

condition.tooth-decay.title: Tooth decay
condition.tooth-decay.summary: Damage to a tooth's surface, or enamel, which happens when bacteria in the mouth make acids that attack the enamel.
condition.tooth-decay.location: A complete permanent set has 32 teeth.

condition.salivary-disorders.title: Salivary gland disorders
condition.salivary-disorders.summary: Problems affecting the three pairs of major salivary glands and hundreds of minor ones, which make saliva and empty it into the mouth through ducts.
condition.salivary-disorders.location: The submandibular glands are one of the three pairs of major salivary glands.

condition.muscle-strain.title: Muscle strain
condition.muscle-strain.summary: A stretched or torn muscle or tendon. Back and hamstring muscle strains are common.
condition.muscle-strain.location: The hamstrings are thigh muscles that bend the leg at the knee.

condition.breast-cancer.title: Breast cancer
condition.breast-cancer.summary: Breast cancer is the second most common cancer in women after skin cancer. Mammograms can detect it early, possibly before it has spread.
condition.breast-cancer.location: The breasts are glandular organs on the chest.
condition.breast-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.breast-changes.title: Benign breast changes
condition.breast-changes.summary: Most women have breast changes at some time. Age, hormone levels and medicines can cause lumps, bumps and discharges that are not breast milk. Most breast changes are benign, meaning they are not cancer.
condition.breast-changes.location: The breasts are made of connective tissue, fat and glandular tissue.
condition.breast-changes.not_depicted: Lumps and other changes are not depicted.

condition.tonsillitis.title: Tonsillitis
condition.tonsillitis.summary: Inflammation (swelling) of the tonsils, usually caused by a viral infection; bacterial infections such as strep throat can also cause it. It is most common in children over age two.
condition.tonsillitis.location: The palatine tonsils lie on either side of the throat.
condition.tonsillitis.not_depicted: Swelling and infection are not depicted.

condition.hypothyroidism.title: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid)
condition.hypothyroidism.summary: The thyroid gland does not make enough thyroid hormones to meet the body's needs.
condition.hypothyroidism.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, its two lobes on each side of the trachea.

condition.hyperthyroidism.title: Hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid)
condition.hyperthyroidism.summary: The thyroid gland makes more thyroid hormones than the body needs. With too much thyroid hormone, many of the body's functions speed up.
condition.hyperthyroidism.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, its two lobes on each side of the trachea.

condition.hashimotos.title: Hashimoto's disease
condition.hashimotos.summary: An autoimmune disorder that can cause hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). It is 4 to 10 times more common in women than men.
condition.hashimotos.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, beneath the larynx.
condition.hashimotos.not_depicted: Inflammation and hormone levels are not depicted.

condition.graves.title: Graves' disease
condition.graves.summary: An autoimmune disorder that can cause hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid).
condition.graves.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, beneath the larynx.

condition.thyroid-nodules.title: Thyroid nodules
condition.thyroid-nodules.summary: A thyroid nodule is a growth (lump) in the thyroid gland, caused by an overgrowth of cells. Nodules are very common, and can be benign or thyroid cancer.
condition.thyroid-nodules.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, beneath the larynx.

condition.thyroid-cancer.title: Thyroid cancer
condition.thyroid-cancer.summary: There are four main types: papillary, follicular, medullary and anaplastic. Papillary is the most common, and thyroid cancer found at an early stage can often be treated successfully.
condition.thyroid-cancer.location: The thyroid sits in the neck, its two lobes on each side of the trachea.
condition.thyroid-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.hyperparathyroidism.title: Primary hyperparathyroidism
condition.hyperparathyroidism.summary: One or more parathyroid glands is overactive and makes too much parathyroid hormone. Blood calcium then rises too high, which can lead to problems such as bone thinning and kidney stones.
condition.hyperparathyroidism.location: The four parathyroid glands lie on or near the thyroid gland in the neck.
condition.hyperparathyroidism.not_depicted: Hormone and calcium levels are not depicted.

condition.mumps.title: Mumps
condition.mumps.summary: A contagious disease caused by the mumps virus, which affects the salivary glands. Common signs are puffy cheeks and a tender, swollen jaw from swollen salivary glands under one or both ears. Most people recover completely within 2 weeks; two doses of the MMR vaccine are the best protection.
condition.mumps.location: The parotid glands lie in front of and just below each ear.
condition.mumps.not_depicted: Swelling and infection are not depicted.

condition.salivary-gland-cancer.title: Salivary gland cancer
condition.salivary-gland-cancer.summary: A rare disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the salivary glands. It is a type of head and neck cancer. Most major salivary gland tumors begin in the parotid glands.
condition.salivary-gland-cancer.location: The parotid glands, the largest salivary glands, lie in front of and just below each ear.
condition.salivary-gland-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.hydrocele.title: Hydrocele
condition.hydrocele.summary: A fluid-filled sac in the scrotum. Hydroceles are common in newborn infants and most go away a few months after birth; in adults they usually do not go away on their own. The main symptom is a painless, swollen scrotum.
condition.hydrocele.location: The scrotum is the external sac that contains the testicles.
condition.hydrocele.not_depicted: Fluid and swelling are not depicted.

condition.varicocele.title: Varicocele
condition.varicocele.summary: Swelling of the veins inside the scrotum, along the spermatic cord that holds up the testicles. Damaged valves in these veins let blood back up. Varicoceles are more common in men aged 15 to 25 and are most often on the left side.
condition.varicocele.location: The veins run along the spermatic cord inside the scrotum.

condition.testicular-torsion.title: Testicular torsion
condition.testicular-torsion.summary: Twisting of the spermatic cord, which supports the testes in the scrotum, cutting off the blood supply to the testicle. It causes sudden severe pain and needs surgery as soon as possible; done within 6 hours, most of the testicle can usually be saved.
condition.testicular-torsion.location: The testes lie inside the scrotum.
condition.testicular-torsion.not_depicted: Twisting and blood flow are not depicted.

condition.vulvar-cancer.title: Vulvar cancer
condition.vulvar-cancer.summary: Usually forms slowly over years, most often on the vaginal lips or the sides of the vaginal opening. Infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) causes about half of all vulvar cancers.
condition.vulvar-cancer.location: The vulva is the external female genital organs, around the opening of the vagina.
condition.vulvar-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.vulvodynia.title: Vulvodynia
condition.vulvodynia.summary: Chronic pain of the vulva, lasting at least 3 months, that does not have a clear cause such as an infection or cancer. It is usually described as burning, stinging, irritation or rawness.
condition.vulvodynia.location: The vulva is the external female genital organs, around the opening of the vagina.

condition.bartholin-cyst.title: Bartholin cyst or abscess
condition.bartholin-cyst.summary: A buildup of fluid, which can become infected and form pus, in one of the Bartholin glands. It forms when the gland's small duct gets blocked, making a tender lump on one side of the vaginal opening.
condition.bartholin-cyst.location: The Bartholin glands are on each side of the vaginal opening.
condition.bartholin-cyst.not_depicted: The cyst and swelling are not depicted.

condition.enlarged-adenoids.title: Enlarged adenoids
condition.enlarged-adenoids.summary: Swollen adenoids, a common problem in children. They may be enlarged from birth or while fighting an infection, and can make breathing through the nose hard, causing mouth breathing, snoring, restless sleep, sleep apnea or ear infections.
condition.enlarged-adenoids.location: The adenoids are high up in the throat, just behind the nose.

condition.high-blood-pressure.title: High blood pressure (hypertension)
condition.high-blood-pressure.summary: A common condition in which the force of blood on the walls of the arteries is often too high: consistent readings of 130/80 mm Hg or more. About half of American adults have it. It usually causes no symptoms until it leads to serious health problems; controlling it can help prevent or delay heart attack, heart failure, stroke and chronic kidney disease.
condition.high-blood-pressure.location: Blood leaves the heart through the aorta, the body's main artery, and reaches the body through the arteries that branch from it.
condition.high-blood-pressure.not_depicted: Blood pressure and the artery walls are not depicted.

condition.atherosclerosis.title: Atherosclerosis
condition.atherosclerosis.summary: A common disease in which plaque made of cholesterol, fat, blood cells and other substances builds up in the walls of arteries, narrowing them and reducing blood flow. It can affect almost any artery: in the heart it is coronary artery disease, in the neck carotid artery disease, and in the legs peripheral artery disease. Blockages can cause heart attack or stroke.
condition.atherosclerosis.location: Plaque can form in arteries throughout the body, including the aorta and the coronary arteries on the surface of the heart.
condition.atherosclerosis.not_depicted: Plaque, narrowed arteries and blood flow are not depicted.

condition.cardiomyopathy.title: Cardiomyopathy
condition.cardiomyopathy.summary: A disease of the heart muscle that makes it harder for the heart to pump blood. Depending on the type, the muscle may become thicker, stiffer or larger than normal, which can cause an irregular heartbeat or heart failure. It can affect people of any age, including young athletes.
condition.cardiomyopathy.location: The ventricles are the heart's lower chambers, which pump blood to the lungs and the body.
condition.cardiomyopathy.not_depicted: Changes in the heart muscle and pumping are not depicted.

condition.congenital-heart-defects.title: Congenital heart defects
condition.congenital-heart-defects.summary: Heart problems present at birth, and the most common type of birth defect, in about 1 in 100 babies born in the United States. The most common defects involve the inside walls of the heart, its valves, or the large blood vessels that carry blood to and from it. Some need no treatment; others need treatment soon after birth.
condition.congenital-heart-defects.location: A wall, the septum, separates the right and left sides of the heart, and four valves control flow through it.
condition.congenital-heart-defects.not_depicted: Defects of the walls, valves and vessels are not depicted.

condition.sleep-apnea.title: Sleep apnea
condition.sleep-apnea.summary: Breathing stops and restarts many times during sleep. In obstructive sleep apnea, the most common type, the upper airway becomes blocked; obesity, large tonsils or hormone changes can narrow it. In central sleep apnea, the brain does not send the signals needed to breathe. Snoring or gasping during sleep and daytime sleepiness are common signs.
condition.sleep-apnea.location: The upper airway runs through the throat, past the tonsils, to the larynx.
condition.sleep-apnea.not_depicted: The blocked airway and breathing are not depicted.

condition.collapsed-lung.title: Collapsed lung (pneumothorax)
condition.collapsed-lung.summary: Air escapes from the lung and fills the space between the lung and the chest wall, pressing on the lung so it cannot expand fully. Causes include chest injuries and air blisters on the lung that break open; tall, thin people, smokers and people with lung diseases are more at risk. Sharp chest pain made worse by breathing in and shortness of breath are common symptoms.
condition.collapsed-lung.location: Each lung sits inside the chest cavity, against the inside of the chest wall.
condition.collapsed-lung.not_depicted: Air around the lung and the collapsed lung are not depicted.

condition.cystic-fibrosis.title: Cystic fibrosis
condition.cystic-fibrosis.summary: A genetic condition that changes a protein in the body and makes mucus thick and sticky. As mucus builds up, it can cause blockages, damage or infections in the airways, digestive tract and other organs. Survival has improved greatly with newborn screening, medicines, nutrition and lung transplants.
condition.cystic-fibrosis.location: Normal mucus is slippery and protects the airways of the lungs and the digestive tract.
condition.cystic-fibrosis.not_depicted: Mucus and blocked airways are not depicted.

condition.tuberculosis.title: Tuberculosis (TB)
condition.tuberculosis.summary: An infection caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It usually affects the lungs, but can also affect other parts of the body such as the brain, kidneys or spine. In inactive TB the germs live in the body without causing illness or spreading; without treatment it can become active TB disease, which can be fatal if not treated properly.
condition.tuberculosis.location: TB usually affects the lungs; it can also affect the lymph nodes and other organs.
condition.tuberculosis.not_depicted: Infection and lung damage are not depicted.

condition.pulmonary-fibrosis.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
condition.pulmonary-fibrosis.summary: A serious long-term disease in which the tissue around the air sacs of the lungs becomes thick and stiff for unknown reasons, causing permanent scarring that makes breathing progressively harder. Shortness of breath and cough are the most common symptoms; the risk is higher with smoking, a family history and age.
condition.pulmonary-fibrosis.location: The tiny air sacs (alveoli) lie inside both lungs, at the ends of the branching airways.
condition.pulmonary-fibrosis.not_depicted: Scarring and stiffened lung tissue are not depicted.

condition.kidney-infection.title: Kidney infection (pyelonephritis)
condition.kidney-infection.summary: A type of urinary tract infection that often begins in the bladder and moves into one or both kidneys, most often caused by bacteria. Symptoms may include fever, pain in the back, side or groin, and painful urination. Early treatment prevents most complications.
condition.kidney-infection.location: Urine flows from the kidneys through the ureters to the bladder.
condition.kidney-infection.not_depicted: Infection and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.urinary-incontinence.title: Bladder control problems (urinary incontinence)
condition.urinary-incontinence.summary: Problems with the way a person holds or releases urine; urinary incontinence is when urine leaks accidentally. Childbirth, menopause, aging and other factors can contribute in women, and aging and prostate problems in men. Treatment depends on the type.
condition.urinary-incontinence.location: The bladder stores urine, which leaves the body through the urethra.
condition.urinary-incontinence.not_depicted: Bladder control and leakage are not depicted.

condition.ibs.title: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
condition.ibs.summary: A group of symptoms that occur together: repeated pain in the abdomen and changes in bowel movements (diarrhea, constipation or both), without visible signs of damage or disease in the digestive tract. It is a disorder of gut-brain interaction that can make the gut more sensitive and change how the bowel muscles contract.
condition.ibs.location: The colon is the main part of the large intestine; the small intestine empties into it.
condition.ibs.not_depicted: Bowel sensitivity and muscle contractions are not depicted.

condition.inguinal-hernia.title: Inguinal hernia
condition.inguinal-hernia.summary: Contents of the abdomen, most often fat or part of the small intestine, bulge through a weak area in the lower abdominal wall at one of the two inguinal canals in the groin. The lining of the abdominal cavity forms a sac around the bulge.
condition.inguinal-hernia.location: The inguinal canals pass through the lower abdominal wall, which is made of layered muscles, one canal on each side of the groin.
condition.inguinal-hernia.not_depicted: The inguinal canals and the hernia are not depicted.

condition.gastritis.title: Gastritis
condition.gastritis.summary: The stomach lining is inflamed. Most people with gastritis have no symptoms; some have indigestion or bleeding in the stomach. Infection with Helicobacter pylori bacteria is the most common cause.
condition.gastritis.location: The stomach lies in the upper left of the abdomen and receives food from the esophagus.
condition.gastritis.not_depicted: Inflammation of the stomach lining is not depicted.

condition.huntingtons.title: Huntington's disease
condition.huntingtons.summary: An inherited disease that causes certain nerve cells in the brain to waste away. Symptoms usually appear in middle age, starting with uncontrolled movements, clumsiness and balance problems; later it can take away the ability to walk, talk and swallow. A person whose parent has it has a 50% chance of getting it. There is no cure, but medicines can help manage some symptoms.
condition.huntingtons.location: Huntington's disease causes certain nerve cells in the brain to waste away.
condition.huntingtons.not_depicted: The affected nerve cells and movements are not depicted.

condition.als.title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
condition.als.summary: A disease of the nervous system, often called Lou Gehrig's disease, that attacks motor neurons, the nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord that send messages to the voluntary muscles. It gets worse over time: as the motor neurons die, the muscles become weak, twitch and waste away. Symptoms most often begin between ages 55 and 75.
condition.als.location: Motor neurons are found in the brain and the spinal cord.
condition.als.not_depicted: Motor neurons and muscle weakness are not depicted.

condition.spinal-stenosis.title: Spinal stenosis
condition.spinal-stenosis.summary: The spaces in the spine narrow and press on the spinal cord and the nerve roots that branch from it. The narrowing usually happens over time and can involve the spinal canal at the center of the vertebrae or the openings through which nerves leave the spine.
condition.spinal-stenosis.location: The spinal cord and nerve roots run through the spinal canal, the hollow space formed by the vertebrae.
condition.spinal-stenosis.not_depicted: Narrowing and pressure on the nerves are not depicted.

condition.sciatica.title: Sciatica
condition.sciatica.summary: Pain, weakness, numbness or tingling in the leg caused by pressure on or injury to the sciatic nerve, which starts in the lower back and runs down the back of each leg. It is a symptom rather than a condition by itself; common causes include a herniated disk and spinal stenosis. The pain is usually on one side.
condition.sciatica.location: The sciatic nerve starts in the lower back, near the lumbar vertebrae.
condition.sciatica.not_depicted: The sciatic nerve and pressure on it are not depicted.

condition.hip-fracture.title: Hip fracture
condition.hip-fracture.summary: A break in the bones of the hip, where the thigh bone (femur) meets the pelvis. It takes great force to hurt a healthy hip, but falls can cause fractures. Osteoporosis of the hip, which is common in older people, causes weak bones that break easily.
condition.hip-fracture.location: The hip is a ball-and-socket joint: a ball at the top of the femur fits into a socket in the pelvis.
condition.hip-fracture.not_depicted: The fracture and the hip joint are not depicted.

condition.patellar-dislocation.title: Kneecap (patellar) dislocation
condition.patellar-dislocation.summary: The kneecap moves fully out of the groove it glides in as the knee bends and straightens; sliding partway out is called a subluxation. Most dislocations are toward the outside of the knee, caused by a hit to the knee or a sudden twisting movement, and they are more common in contact sports. It can happen more than once.
condition.patellar-dislocation.location: The kneecap sits within the quadriceps tendon, in a groove at the front of the lower end of the thigh bone.
condition.patellar-dislocation.not_depicted: The displaced kneecap is not depicted.

condition.osgood-schlatter.title: Osgood-Schlatter disease
condition.osgood-schlatter.summary: A painful swelling of the bump on the upper part of the shinbone, just below the knee. It is thought to come from small injuries caused by overuse before the knee has finished growing, when the strong quadriceps muscle is used a lot in sports during a growth spurt. It is common in adolescents who run and jump.
condition.osgood-schlatter.location: The patellar ligament connects the kneecap to the bump at the top of the front of the shinbone.
condition.osgood-schlatter.not_depicted: Swelling of the shinbone is not depicted.

condition.tmd.title: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD)
condition.tmd.summary: More than 30 conditions that affect the temporomandibular joints (TMJs) and can cause pain, stiffness and trouble chewing in the jaw joint and the muscles that control jaw movement. The main types are disorders of the jaw joints, disorders of the chewing muscles, and headaches from a TMD. Many last only a short time and go away on their own.
condition.tmd.location: The two temporomandibular joints, one on each side of the jaw, connect the lower jaw (mandible) to the skull; the chewing muscles move it.
condition.tmd.not_depicted: The jaw joints, pain and joint problems are not depicted.

condition.refractive-errors.title: Refractive errors (nearsightedness and farsightedness)
condition.refractive-errors.summary: The most common type of vision problem: the shape of the eye keeps light from focusing correctly on the retina, so it is hard to see clearly. The common types are nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism and presbyopia. Glasses or contact lenses can help people see clearly.
condition.refractive-errors.location: The cornea and the lens focus light onto the retina at the back of the eye.
condition.refractive-errors.not_depicted: The shape of the eye and the focusing of light are not depicted.

condition.lymphoma.title: Lymphoma
condition.lymphoma.summary: Cancer that begins in cells of the lymph system. The two main types are Hodgkin lymphoma, which can often be cured, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, whose outlook depends on its specific type.
condition.lymphoma.location: Lymph nodes lie along the lymphatic pathways; the spleen and thymus are also lymphatic organs.
condition.lymphoma.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.leukemia.title: Leukemia
condition.leukemia.summary: Cancers of the blood cells. The type depends on which blood cell becomes cancer and whether it grows quickly or slowly. It occurs most often in adults older than 55, but it is also the most common cancer in children younger than 15.
condition.leukemia.location: Red bone marrow contains the blood stem cells that become red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets; it fills the small cavities of spongy bone.
condition.leukemia.not_depicted: Bone marrow and blood cells are not depicted.

condition.laryngeal-cancer.title: Laryngeal cancer
condition.laryngeal-cancer.summary: Cancer that forms in the tissues of the larynx, a type of head and neck cancer. Using tobacco and drinking too much alcohol affect the risk. A sore throat or cough that does not go away, trouble swallowing, ear pain, a lump in the neck or throat, or a change in the voice are reasons to check with a doctor.
condition.laryngeal-cancer.location: The larynx has three parts: the supraglottis, above the vocal cords, including the epiglottis; the glottis, where the vocal cords are; and the subglottis, between the vocal cords and the trachea.
condition.laryngeal-cancer.not_depicted: Tumors and their spread are not depicted.

condition.pid.title: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
condition.pid.summary: An infection of a woman's reproductive organs, often a complication of sexually transmitted infections such as chlamydia and gonorrhea; other infections can also cause it. About 1 in 8 women with a history of PID have difficulty getting pregnant.
condition.pid.location: The female reproductive organs include the uterus, the fallopian tubes and the ovaries.
condition.pid.not_depicted: Infection and inflammation are not depicted.

condition.ankylosing-spondylitis.title: Ankylosing spondylitis
condition.ankylosing-spondylitis.summary: A type of arthritis that causes inflammation in the joints and ligaments of the spine, leading to stiffness. In severe cases the vertebrae can fuse, making the spine rigid. It can also affect joints such as the knees, ankles and hips, and some people develop eye disease (uveitis) or skin disease.
condition.ankylosing-spondylitis.location: The vertebral column runs from the base of the skull to the tailbone.
condition.ankylosing-spondylitis.not_depicted: Inflammation and fused vertebrae are not depicted.

condition.hearing-loss.title: Hearing loss
condition.hearing-loss.summary: Causes include heredity, diseases such as ear infections and meningitis, injury, certain medicines, long-term exposure to loud noise and aging. There are two main types: one happens when the inner ear or the auditory nerve is damaged; the other when sound waves cannot reach the inner ear, for example because of earwax, fluid or a punctured eardrum, and treatment or surgery can often reverse it.
condition.hearing-loss.location: Sound waves reach the inner ear, which connects to the brain through the auditory nerve.
condition.hearing-loss.not_depicted: The ear and hearing are not depicted.

condition.ear-infection.title: Ear infections (otitis media)
condition.ear-infection.summary: The most common reason parents bring a child to a doctor: three out of four children have at least one ear infection by their third birthday. Adults can also get them, but less often. The infection usually affects the middle ear, and often goes away on its own.
condition.ear-infection.location: Ear infections usually affect the middle ear.
condition.ear-infection.not_depicted: The ear and the infection are not depicted.

condition.sinusitis.title: Sinusitis (sinus infection)
condition.sinusitis.summary: The sinuses are inflamed, from an infection or another problem. Acute sinusitis often starts as a cold that turns into a bacterial infection; allergies, nasal problems and certain diseases can also cause it. Symptoms can include fever, weakness, fatigue, cough, congestion and mucus draining down the back of the throat.
condition.sinusitis.location: The sinuses are hollow air spaces within the bones surrounding the nose.
condition.sinusitis.not_depicted: The sinuses and their inflammation are not depicted.
